To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the institutionalization of internal CSR is shaped by the institutional settings of home and host countries, and by the institutional logics of the firm's headquarters and subsidiaries.

The institutional framework of the home and host countries is a key factor influencing the regulatory and distributives spheres, whereas the spheres of discretionary and soft policies are shaped by the MNEs, and may also by guided by intergovernment institutions and NGOs.

the institutional configuration of CSR in MNC operating in Canada and in Brazil is influenced by the institutional settings of the home and host countries, as well as by the headquarters subsidiary relations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interplay between the MNC's home and host institutional environments and its internal CSR.
the interplay between home and host countries institutional settings and the role played by headquarters and subsidiaries in the development of internal CSR.
the role of institutions in the development of internal CSR in multinational corporations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

internal CSR institutionalization is a dynamic and complex process that is influenced by the institutional orders of the home and host countries, as well as by the institutional logics of the MNC and its subsidiaries.
CSR is a process of institutionalization and that it is embedded in a complex web of institutional logics.

the institutional configuration of CSR in MNC operations in the two countries is influenced by the MNC's headquarters subsidiary relations within its home country and host countries institutional settings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the institutional logics of the host and home countries and of headquarters and subsidiaries, as well as of MNCs, are key to the development of internal CSR.
CSR in MNC subsidiaries is a complex process of institutional alignment, with multiple stakeholders, institutional orders, and logics at play.
the institutional logics perspective offers a systematic and useful framework to understand how CSR is institutionalized in the context of MNCs operating across multiple countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CSR reality in the mining sector is not as simple as the dichotomy of the North-South divide.
the institutional logics of home and host countries play an important role in shaping CSR practices in MNCs.
the MNC's internal CSR is influenced by the institutional setting of the host country, the MNCs' home country, and the intergovernmental institutional setting.
